limitations: The closed bundle can establish only the recorded preregistration and result-access ordering; it cannot independently prove the absence of unrecorded external result access.

Fresh installation, pytest, Ruff, and upstream repository commands were not rerun in this restricted audit session; their manifest-bound captures, complete byte closures, and retained rebuilt wheel were independently replayed.

findings.rationale: The live runner checks pidfd, /proc executable, argv, nonce, and direct pipes before reading output, but the importer later receives ordinary same-UID attempt directories and validates only caller-writable process.json assertions. validate_execution_attestation does not retain or replay a live pidfd, /proc state, or an independently authenticated nonce, so a prebuilt fixed-root attempt can synthesize all checked metadata and mint accepted R0-R2 receipts without a Codex launch.
findings.required_action: Require an importer-controlled live handoff from the runner or a signature/MAC issued by a separately protected authority over the launch, direct-pipe transcript, output, and nonce. Do not accept post-hoc same-UID attempt directories as proof of execution.
findings.title: Persisted AI execution attestations are forgeable post-hoc metadata

findings.rationale: The fixed R3 importer and generic-R3 denial create the intended structural transition, but the R3 importer inherits the forgeable process.json attestation. A same-UID caller can construct two fixed-root R3 attempts and thereby manufacture the protected acceptance prerequisite.
findings.required_action: Bind R3 acceptance to unforgeable live-runner provenance and make authorization replay that protected provenance, not merely hashes and declarative fields from caller-writable attempt files.
findings.title: The fixed R3 transition lacks authentic protected-run provenance

findings.rationale: The denominator, topology, fixed-input, and one-use consumption controls are present, but the required approval provenance remains forgeable because the test-access importer accepts post-hoc fixed-root attempts whose execution attestations are ordinary caller-writable JSON.
findings.required_action: Require an unforgeable protected AI-run receipt for both test-access primaries before producing or consuming the one-use full-test approval.
findings.title: Full-test approval is not authenticated to actual protected AI executions

findings.rationale: The dedicated importer replays events, output, model, reasoning, bundle, and fixed paths, but all of those bytes and the process attestation can be prebuilt by the same UID in the expected audit root. Directory and file modes do not establish issuer authenticity.
findings.required_action: Make the test-access importer consume an importer-controlled live runner channel or cryptographically authenticated execution receipt that a workspace author cannot synthesize.
findings.title: A synthetic protected-attempt directory can still authorize full-test access

findings.rationale: Direct completion clients now route through the fixed post-R3 gate, but that gate accepts the fixed R3 receipt produced from forgeable post-hoc attempt metadata. Manufacturing that receipt therefore makes completion transports reachable without an actual protected R3 acceptance.
findings.required_action: Require every post-R3 provider boundary to replay an unforgeable protected R3 execution chain, including live launch identity and output continuity, before allowing any completion request.
findings.title: Completion clients can be unlocked with a forged protected R3 receipt

parent_finding_closures.rationale: Authorization now consumes fixed candidate-bound artifacts and recomputes bundle, source, environment, model, ledger, and receipt identities; release remains unconditionally fail-closed.

The importer validates comprehensive bytes but trusts a post-hoc process.json attestation that the same UID can synthesize; it therefore cannot prove that the asserted Codex process or direct-pipe execution occurred.

The response schema and importer separate revise/no-call from acceptance, and accepted receipts require the exact bootstrap disposition, all stages accepted, all parent findings closed, and zero open P0/P1.
The active validator explicitly requires candidate.4, recomputes its complete 438-entry inventory, parses strict gate semantics, and rejects reused or mismatched artifacts.
The append-only snapshot chain validates legal transitions, immutable finalization, per-call native IDs, unknown outcomes, exact slots, and journaling before response interpretation.

The closure now contains every runner/helper and Runtime wheel input, including py.typed, CSS, JavaScript, and HTML data; exact wheel/source paths and bytes match, and the retained independent rebuild has the same digest.
The fixed R3 transition exists, but its prerequisite can be manufactured from synthetic fixed-root attempts because its stored execution attestation lacks an independent issuer.

Dataset, strata, denominator, topology, and one-use controls are closed, but the AI approval receipt is not authenticated to an actual protected process and can be minted from synthetic attempt files.
The frozen manifest binds 216 exact case IDs, categories, languages, denominators, adapter, worker, dependencies, execution identity, and per-case ledger replay before accepted result access.
Serving cells are rebuilt from fixed raw receipts and the globally reconciled ledger with workload, identity, topology, and native-request uniqueness checks; absent active inputs fail closed.
The schema truthfully identifies AI authority, closed-set limitations, xhigh reasoning, permitted stages, and the distinction between bootstrap disposition and later authorization.

The active six-entry hash-chained ledger is the reconciled current R0-R2 state source and cross-checks subordinate candidate/source identities and legal transitions; older ledgers remain preserved as historical evidence.

Authorization uses the fixed importer aggregate and replays two distinct raw-event/output bindings rather than accepting standalone caller-selected stage receipts; the remaining protected-run authenticity defect is tracked under DG10-C3-AI-002.
The dedicated importer checks the requested fields, but its process provenance remains caller-writable and can be synthesized without an actual protected AI execution.
Exactly 24 immutable slot IDs, one candidate-global capability, one fixed ledger, atomic slot/provider claims, and aggregate replay/concurrency rejection are implemented.
The previously absent source and all active worker inputs are materialized in the complete current inventory and match the execution closure byte-for-byte.
The immutable amendment and active acceptance/validation artifacts consistently require gpt-5.6-sol with xhigh reasoning and give the interrupted max attempt no effect.
The independently rebuilt wheel is retained in the bundle, content-addressed, and byte-identical to the installed source wheel.
The sole full-test boundary atomically records one-use consumption before invoking the callback, revalidates afterward, and rejects repeat or concurrent execution.
The captures use explicit pytest and Ruff configuration paths whose digest is bound in the active closure, with 259 tests passing and Ruff reporting all checks passed.

Provider access is sealed behind one adapter, with an O_EXCL provider claim persisted before the request, raw response and native ID journaled before semantic parsing, and adversarial aggregate-concurrency coverage.
The active records use timezone-aware ordered timestamps: worker and execution identities precede the case-manifest freeze, which precedes any accepted result-access timestamp required by scoring.
The R1 validation receipt embeds the complete active 438-entry source inventory, and stage-ledger replay compares subordinate candidate and source identities before accepting the binding.

Completion-capable code routes through the fixed boundary, but its post-R3 authorization can be unlocked by a forged R3 importer receipt because protected execution provenance is not independently authenticated.
The CLI registers one attempt-ledger option, and parser/import regression coverage is present in the collected passing suite.
The preflight returns phase-specific success statuses, including zero for successful post-R3 validation, with regression coverage in the passing capture.

reproduction_commands: jq -r '.entries[] | [.sha256,.path] | @tsv' review-manifest.json | while IFS=$'\t' read -r digest path; do test "$(sha256sum -- "$path" | cut -d' ' -f1)" = "$digest" || printf '%s\n' "$path"; done
jq -r '.entries[] | [.size,.path] | @tsv' review-manifest.json | while IFS=$'\t' read -r size path; do test "$(stat -c %s -- "$path")" = "$size" || printf '%s\n' "$path"; done

find current-source -type f -print0 | sort -z | while IFS= read -r -d '' path; do relative=${path#current-source/}; digest=$(sha256sum -- "$path" | cut -d' ' -f1); printf '%s\0%s\0' "$relative" "$digest"; done | sha256sum

DG10-R0.rationale: The candidate.2 archive receipt, controls, 201 safe members, immutable NO-GO, complete registers, and succession history replay exactly. Nevertheless, DG10-C3-AI-002 remains an open P0 applicable to imported R0 acceptance, so the policy forbids an ACCEPTED stage decision.

DG10-R1.rationale: Claim validation, append-only call accounting, exact 24-slot enforcement, fixed paths, one-use test access, and unconditional release denial are materially strong. R1 is not closed because all three AI importers trust forgeable post-hoc execution attestations, allowing synthetic R0-R2, test-access, or R3 authority.

DG10-R2.rationale: The retained wheel rebuild is byte-identical, all 65 Runtime payloads match source including package data, the 395-entry execution/config closure and 192-entry BFCL tree replay, and the captured fresh install, 259-test collection/run, and Ruff checks are coherent. ACCEPTED is still prohibited while parent P0/P1 findings affecting independent receipt authenticity remain open.
